candidate.selection_reason: Changed function signature to accept object parameter -> enables enhanced prototype pollution protection -> prevents access to unsafe inherited properties
candidate.source_summary: The function validates property names for objects used in math expression parsing and evaluation. The 'object' parameter is typically a plain object (scope, math namespace, or object node properties) that may contain user-defined or built-in properties. The 'prop' parameter is a string property name that may come from parsed expression syntax (e.g., object property access like 'obj.constructor').
candidate.sink_summary: The validation result (true/false) controls whether property access is allowed in getSafeProperty/setSafeProperty and object node compilation. If unsafe, an error is thrown preventing access to dangerous inherited properties like constructor, toString, call, apply, or ghosted properties.
candidate.guard_summary: The function implements multiple security checks: 1) Rejects non-objects; 2) Rejects 'ghosted' properties (own property that also exists in prototype); 3) Allows whitelisted native properties (e.g., 'length'); 4) Rejects properties inherited from Object.prototype; 5) Rejects properties inherited from Function.prototype. These controls aim to prevent prototype pollution and access to dangerous inherited methods.
candidate.risk_pattern: Property access validation that prevents access to inherited prototype properties which could lead to prototype pollution, property hijacking, or unintended method invocation when user-controlled property names reach object property access operations.
used_variable_sources: object parameter (scope, math namespace, or object properties)
prop parameter (property name from parsed expression)
called_function_context: isSafeProperty is called by ObjectNode.compile for validating object property keys
enclosing_conditions: Called within compileObjectNode during expression compilation
Preceded by hasOwnProperty check on node.properties
candidate.context_summary: isSafeProperty is part of a security utility module used throughout the math expression engine to safely access and modify object properties. It works alongside getSafeProperty and setSafeProperty to prevent access to dangerous inherited properties. The changed function signature now accepts an object parameter, enabling enhanced prototype pollution protection by checking ghosted properties and prototype inheritance relative to the specific object.
unresolved_facts: Exact data flow of user-controlled property names into isSafeProperty calls
Whether all call sites pass the object parameter correctly after the change
Whether safeNativeProperties whitelist is comprehensive for all safe cases
Whether there are other prototype chains beyond Object and Function that need checking
